title: Developmental timing of sudden unexpected infant death
research_questions: What is the developmental timing of sudden unexpected infant death?
data_sources_used: linked birth and infant death records

variables.operationalization: underlying cause of death codes R95, R99 and W75
variables.quote: sudden unexpected infant death, defined by underlying cause of death codes R95, R99 and W75
with age at death in days

variables.operationalization: gestational age at birth plus chronological age
variables.quote: aligned infants by postconceptional age (gestational age at birth plus chronological age)

variables.operationalization: not specified, but implied as a stratifying variable for risk analysis
variables.quote: Male excess risk emerged only after 44 weeks postconceptional age

variables.operationalization: not specified, but implied as an exposure variable affecting timing of risk onset

claims.statement: The study used linked birth and infant death records to examine sudden unexpected infant death.
claims.quote: We used linked birth and infant death records.

claims.statement: Male infants showed an excess risk of sudden unexpected infant death after reaching 44 weeks postconceptional age.
claims.quote: Male excess risk emerged only after 44 weeks postconceptional age.

claims.statement: Prenatal smoking was associated with an earlier onset of the risk for sudden unexpected infant death.
claims.quote: Prenatal smoking was associated with earlier onset of risk.

claims.statement: The study lacked information on the sleep environment, which is not available in the linked birth-death files.
claims.quote: A limitation is that the sleep environment was not available in the linked birth-death files.
